transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I've been really struggling lately because I keep getting these intense, horrible memories of a bad event from my past that just crash into my mind. Sometimes it feels so real, like I'm actually back there reliving it all over again, and I just can't make it stop.
I'm so sorry you are experiencing this. Could you tell me when this difficult event occurred and how long you have been having these intense memories?

The event happened about six months ago, and I've been dealing with these awful memories constantly ever since. It's been a non-stop struggle for the past six months, and I just feel so exhausted from reliving it every single day.
Do you find yourself actively trying to avoid thoughts, feelings, people, or places that remind you of what happened?

Yes, I do everything I can to push those thoughts and feelings out of my mind because it's just too painful to face them. I also completely avoid certain places and people that might trigger those memories, just to keep myself from reliving it.
Have you also noticed changes in your mood or reactivity, such as feeling constantly on edge, easily startled, irritable, or having trouble sleeping?

Yes, I've been feeling extremely irritable and on edge lately, often snapping at people for the smallest reasons. My sleep has also been terrible; I struggle to fall asleep, wake up constantly from bad dreams, and always feel completely unrefreshed.
Without going into too much painful detail, could you tell me if this event involved a threat to your life, serious injury, or your physical safety?
It's really hard for me to talk about the details of what happened. I can say it was terrifying and I felt completely unsafe, but I'd prefer not to go into the specifics of it right now.
Since this event, have you noticed changes in how you view yourself or the world, or do you feel disconnected from the people around you?

Yes, I feel completely damaged and worthless now, and I feel like the world is entirely dangerous and no one can be trusted. I also feel totally numb inside, completely disconnected from others and unable to feel love or affection even for my own family.

latest_inference.note: The patient meets the full DSM-5 diagnostic criteria for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), including intrusion symptoms (flashbacks, nightmares), avoidance behavior, negative alterations in cognitions and mood (feeling worthless, detached, unable to experience positive emotions), and marked alterations in arousal and reactivity (irritability, hypervigilance, sleep disturbance), all persisting for six months following a terrifying event. Because the criteria for PTSD are fully met, Adjustment Disorder is ruled out.
